communication.wish_model: Wishing you joy and laughter from January to December!
wish_suggestions: happy days from January to December
a life full of happy moments

picture_customs.activity: go to Times Square to watch the New Year's Eve Ball drop

world_customs.activity: put 12 grapes in their mouth at midnight
drop ice cream on the floor

passages.speaker: Russ
passages.text: I often go to Times Square with my parents to welcome the New Year. When the clock strikes midnight, colourful fireworks light up the sky. Everybody cheers and sings.

passages.speaker: Wu
passages.text: On New Year's Day, we dress beautifully and go to our grandparents' houses. We wish them Happy New Year and they give us lucky money. Then we go out and have a day full of fun.

passages.speaker: Mai
passages.text: I learn some customs about Tet from my parents. People give rice to wish for enough food and buy salt to wish for good luck. Dogs are lucky animals but cats are not. A cat's cry sounds like ‘poor’ in Vietnamese.

who_statements.statement: We give rice to wish for enough food.
who_statements.speaker: Mai

visible_questions.question: What do they throw away before Tet?
What do they clean and decorate?

replacement_audio.script: Nguyen is writing to Tom about Tet. Before Tet, his family throws away old things. They clean and decorate their house with peach flowers. They buy new clothes and cakes. His mother cooks banh chung. The children get lucky money in red envelopes and make wishes for good luck. They should behave well and shouldn't break anything.

writing_prompts: Children should help decorate the house.

advice_sentences.cue: ask for permission before entering a room
ask for some water if thirsty

project.title: I wish
steps: Each student gets a small piece of paper and writes his or her wishes on it.
He or she hangs it on a tree.
Other students take turns to get a piece of paper and read the wish aloud.
The class guesses whose wish it is.
example_wishes: I want to have a brother.
I want to live in a tree house.
now_i_can: use words related to things and activities at Tet
use should and shouldn't for advice
use some and any for amount
talk about what children should and shouldn't do at Tet
listen and write an email about Tet preparations
